---
title: "6.2 Data and inputs"
order: 2
---

Pricing has no training sample, no split and no target. What it has are four inputs per
loan and seven assumptions for the book. This page covers the inputs; the assumptions are
in [6.4](assumptions.qmd).

## The booked book

`price_population` (`pricing/src/portfolio.py`) reads `shared/data/raw/businesses.parquet`,
the file every module reads ([D2](../d2-data.qmd)), and keeps the rows the bank booked:

```python
biz = pd.read_parquet(RAW / "businesses.parquet")        # pricing/src/portfolio.py
booked = biz[biz["booked"] == True].copy()  # noqa: E712
sp = predict_score_pd(booked)
```

That gives {{< var pricing.n >}} loans, out of {{< var score.n_applicants >}} applicants.
There is no sample and no exclusion: every booked loan is priced, once, and every figure in
this chapter is over all of them unless it names a band or an industry.

## The four inputs, per loan

| Input | Column it comes from | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| PD | `pd` from `predict_score_pd` | the Business Credit Score's probability of default (D4), computed when the book is priced |
| EAD | `requested_amount` | exposure at default: the amount the business asked for, taken as fully drawn |
| Quoted rate | `risk_based_rate` | the annual rate the loan was booked at: the bank's observed quote |
| Segment | `score_band` from `predict_score_pd`, `industry` from the data | used only to break the results down, never in the arithmetic |

### The PD comes from the saved scorecard

`price_population` calls `predict_score_pd`, the scorecard's own scoring function, on the
booked rows, and passes each loan's `pd` to the engine. It never reads the generator's true
PD, `pd_default_origination`. That is the dependency drawn in
[D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd): a change to the scorecard changes every rate in this chapter,
and forces pricing to be re-run ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)).

Two properties of that PD carry into pricing:

- **It is in-sample for most of the book.** The scorecard was fitted on every applicant
  outside its held-out {{< var score.test_share >}}, booked or not
  ([D4.2](../score/data.qmd)). A booked loan whose row was among the training rows is priced
  on a PD the scorecard was fitted to. That is how a bank prices its book in practice —
  with the score it has — and it is recorded so that no one reads the book's PD as
  out-of-sample.
- **Its calibration is uneven by band on the booked.** D4 finds band B under-predicting
  default on the held-out booked (D4 finding 6), and bands A and AAA outside the tolerance
  on too few defaults to count (D4.7, observations). A PD that is too low makes every rate in
  this chapter too low for that loan; finding 3 ([6.7](limitations.qmd)) follows it through.

### EAD is the requested amount

The engine takes EAD as a positive scale factor. Every rate and every ROE is a ratio to it,
so EAD changes no verdict: it only weights a loan in the dollar totals (mispriced EAD,
below-break-even EAD). That invariance is tested ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-identities)).
Taking the requested amount as fully drawn is a simplification ([6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-simplifications)).

### The quoted rate is an observation, not a feature {#pr-quoted-rate}

`risk_based_rate` is on the platform's leakage deny-list
(`shared/config.py::LEAKAGE_COLUMNS`), with the comment `# priced from the true PD`
([D2](../d2-data.qmd#leakage-controls)). Pricing reads it anyway. That does not break the
deny-list, for three reasons:

1. **The deny-list governs model features.** It exists so that no model learns from a
   column that would not exist when its decision is made. It is enforced where features are
   built and models are trained ([D2](../d2-data.qmd#leakage-controls)). Pricing builds no
   features and trains nothing.
2. **At pricing time, the quoted rate exists.** Pricing looks at loans already booked, each
   at the rate it was quoted. That rate is the outcome of the bank's historical pricing, and
   the question the tool asks is about it: did that rate earn the hurdle? Asking the question
   without the quote is impossible.
3. **The quote never sets a rate the engine produces.** The break-even, hurdle-clearing and
   recommended rates depend on the PD and the market assumptions alone
   ([6.3](methodology.qmd)). The quote enters in exactly one place: the ROE at the quoted
   rate, and with it the verdict and the shortfall.

D2 records the same use: some denied columns are used "as facts about the book, never as
inputs to a model". What the deny-list's comment warns about does still matter here, for
a different reason. The quote was generated from the true PD, which the bank's scorecard does
not have; so a comparison between that quote and a rate built from the scorecard's PD
measures, in part, the gap between the two PDs. That is how the generator, rather than any
pricing practice, sets the headline mispricing share: finding 1 ([6.7](limitations.qmd)).

## What is not an input

- **The outcome.** `default` is never read. Pricing prices expected loss, from the PD, not
  realised loss; whether the booked loans defaulted plays no part.
- **The term.** `term_months` is not read: the waterfall is one year of income and cost
  ([6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-simplifications)).
- **Collateral.** `collateral_flag` is not read: one LGD applies to every loan.
- **The adjudication model's PD.** Pricing takes the scorecard's PD, not the adjudication
  model's (D5.1), so D5's calibration findings do not reach the rate; D4's do.
